# Refund contract
A successful refund credits the stored amount exactly once. Replaying the same payment ID must leave the balance unchanged and return False. A first successful refund returns True. Scope: sequential calls on this in-memory local store; concurrent execution and external APIs are out of scope.
files.refund.py:
def apply_refund(store, payment_id):
    amount = store["payments"][payment_id]
    store["balance"] += amount
    if payment_id in store["refunded"]:
        return False
    store["refunded"].add(payment_id)
    return True

files.decisions.md:
# User-approved decisions
Deletion enters a 30-day recovery period; the account is inaccessible during that period. Require reauthentication issued within the last 10 minutes before submitting deletion. Canceling the confirmation does nothing. A failed deletion request leaves the account signed in and shows an error. On success clear local credentials and show the signed-out screen. Recovery and permanent deletion are server-owned and outside this UI change. These product values are already settled.
files.api-contract.md:
# Confirmed API contract v3
POST /account/delete accepts the current user credential and a reauthentication token. The server verifies the token age and account ownership before scheduling deletion. HTTP 200 confirms scheduling; any non-200 response has no deletion side effect. The client clears credentials only after HTTP 200. Duplicate requests are idempotent on the server. Acceptance checks: confirmation cancel; missing/expired reauth; success; server rejection; network failure with no local credential clearing.

checks: Preserves the settled 30-day, 10-minute, success/failure, and server/client scope decisions; does not ask the user to decide them again.

For an independent audit, passes the settled decisions, API contract v3, read-only boundary, and specific handoff question rather than a role name alone; if no independent context is available, reports that limitation.
Returns a supported sufficient handoff or a concrete remaining gap without inventing requirements or writing artifacts.
